HasUponPickupEffect.rationale: Matches GoldenCompass.cs:17. Shadowed by ANCIENT rarity in Relic.is_tradable (relics/base.py:132-136), but correct.

AfterObtained.rationale: GoldenCompass.cs:33-37 sets GoldenPathAct = CurrentActIndex then awaits RunManager.Instance.GenerateMap(); golden_compass.py:32-33 sets self.golden_path_act = run.act_index then calls run.regenerate_map(), in the same order -- which matters, because the modifier the regeneration consults is keyed on the field just written. Executed (`py audit/tools/relic_probes_b06.py b06-misc`): `run.add_relic('golden_compass')` on a started act-0 run leaves golden_path_act 0 and a 16-point single-column map. See guard N3 for the one difference in what the regeneration touches besides the map.

ModifyGeneratedMap.rationale: GoldenCompass.cs:39-46 returns the map unchanged unless `GoldenPathAct == actIndex`, and otherwise returns `new GoldenPathActMap(runState)`; golden_compass.py:36-40 is the same guard and returns actmap.golden_path_map(...). The layouts match exactly: GoldenPathActMap's 16 _defaultPointTypes (GoldenPathActMap.cs:9-27) are Monster, Unknown, Monster, RestSite, Monster, RestSite, Unknown, Treasure, Unknown, Treasure, Unknown, Shop, Elite, RestSite, Elite, RestSite, and actmap.py's _GOLDEN_PATH_TYPES is the identical 16-tuple in the same order; width 7 with the column fixed at 3, an ANCIENT starting point at (3, 0) and a BOSS beyond the last row, each row chained to the next. Executed (`py audit/tools/relic_probes_b06.py b06-misc`): the post-pickup map is 16 points in exactly that type order. Correct phase, too -- this is ModifyGeneratedMap and not the Late pass, so it is unaffected by the dispatch-site divergence recorded at relic/fur_coat G2. The dropped `Players.Count > 1` branch is N2 (waived).

ModifyUnknownMapPointRoomTypes.rationale: GoldenCompass.cs:48-55 returns the incoming set unless `GoldenPathAct == RunState.CurrentActIndex` and otherwise returns `new HashSet<RoomType> { RoomType.Event }`; golden_compass.py:43-47 is the same guard and returns `{RoomType.EVENT}`. Note both compare against the CURRENT act rather than against a parameter -- so once the player leaves the golden-path act the '?' nodes behave normally again, on both sides. Executed (`py audit/tools/relic_probes_b06.py b06-misc`): with golden_path_act 0 and the run in act 0, the hook replaces any incoming set with {RoomType.EVENT}. This is the chain hook audit/records/seam/hook_dispatch.json step 32 lists as ModifyUnknownMapPointRoomTypes (Hook.cs:2061) and verdicts faithful; a REPLACING listener makes the chain order matter, but the sim has exactly one implementer (relics/juzu_bracelet.py's is a dropped hook per sweep C, not an implementation), so no ordering question arises today.

guards.what: N1: `GoldenPathAct` initialised to -1 on both sides (GoldenCompass.cs:13; golden_compass.py:28) and never reset
guards.rationale: Per-RUN state by design: C# marks it [SavedProperty] (GoldenCompass.cs:19) so it survives save/load, and nothing assigns it back to -1. sweep-reset lists golden_compass among the 32 never-reset candidates with 'C# resets: NONE (may be per-run by design)', and that reading is right -- the sentinel -1 also guarantees the two modifier hooks are inert before pickup, since no act index is negative. PROMPT.md bug class 13's reader trace is trivial here: the only readers are the two modifier hooks, and both compare for equality with an act index.

guards.what: N2: `if (runState.Players.Count > 1) list.RemoveAt(2)` -- multiplayer drops the third node, shortening the golden path to 15 (GoldenPathActMap.cs:42-45)
guards.rationale: Multiplayer-only: single-player keeps all 16 point types, which is what actmap.py's _GOLDEN_PATH_TYPES hard-codes. Waived under the shared contract's multiplayer exclusion. Recorded rather than skipped because it is a length difference in a fixed layout, so a future multiplayer port must add the branch rather than adjust a number.

guards.what: N3: `run.regenerate_map()` also resets current_point, map_history and _last_room_types (run.py:890-900), where RunManager.GenerateMap sets State.Map and calls State.RemoveStaleVisitedMapCoords(map) (RunManager.cs:753-754)
guards.rationale: Both sides leave the room queues and the '?'-odds alone -- rooms are rolled once per act -- and the sim's docstring says so. The player position agrees: an Ancient relic is obtained at the act's Ancient node, which is row 0 column `_MAP_WIDTH // 2` = 3 on a standard map and (3, 0) on GoldenPathActMap, so `current_point = self.map.starting_point` lands on the same coord C# leaves CurrentMapPoint on. The visited-coord bookkeeping differs in form -- C# PRUNES stale coords and keeps (3, 0), the sim clears map_history outright -- but map_history has no reader that changes behaviour: `grep -rn map_history sts2_rl/` shows the only consumers are conformance/runner.py and conformance/save.py reading the ORACLE's history from the save file, never the sim's own list. Recorded per binding rule 7: this rationale leans on run.py and conformance/runner.py, which this record does NOT hash, so a change there goes stale invisibly.

guards.what: N4 (SETTLED BY EXECUTION): GoldenPathActMap is a fixed layout that consumes NO rng, yet golden_path_map takes an rng argument and RunState._generate_map builds a full StandardMap first
guards.rationale: Binding rule 5 plus PROMPT.md bug class 16: a named-or-passed rng is only a divergence if it is CONSUMED. GoldenPathActMap's constructor (GoldenPathActMap.cs:39-68) contains no Rng use at all, and actmap.golden_path_map (actmap.py:1027-1057) stores `fixed.rng = rng or random.Random()` and never draws from it -- it walks a fixed tuple. The wasted base-map generation is faithful too, and that is the non-obvious half: RunManager.GenerateMap builds `State.Act.CreateMap(State, replaceTreasureWithElites: false)` FIRST (RunManager.cs:745) and only then lets Hook.ModifyGeneratedMap replace it, so the game also burns a full StandardActMap's worth of map draws that Golden Compass discards. Executed (`py audit/tools/relic_probes_b06.py b06-misc`): the shared run rng does advance across the pickup, which is correct rather than a leak.

guards.what: N5: the sim has no `undo_after_obtained` for this relic (relics/base.py:143-150)
guards.rationale: Recorded and dismissed deliberately, because Golden Compass is exactly the shape the undo hook exists for -- a pickup that mutates run state outside run.relics -- and the conformance runner grants a node's relic before swapping it for the one the save recorded, so a golden-pathed map would survive the swap. That is a sim-only concern with NO C# counterpart (nothing in the game ever un-picks a relic; the base docstring says so), so it is not a source-to-sim divergence and cannot be a gap on this record. Flagged for the conformance stream rather than verdicted here.
